 THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 29.07.2017 PASSED IN MVC NO.53/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE & AMACT, KARKALA, AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.7,65,200/- WITH INTEREST AT 8%
P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL THE DATE OF REALIZATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the Insurance Company challenged the judgment and award dated 29.09.2017 in M.V.C.No.83/2017 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T., Karkala ('the Tribunal' for short).
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

Brief facts of the case are, on 07.09.2016 at about 09:45 pm, the husband of 1st petitioner, father of petitioners No.2 to 5 by name Sundara Naik, the deceased, while walking near Jayaram Bhat Conventional Hall towards Yennehole on Karkala- Ajekar State Highway, a Maruti Omni bearing Reg.No.KA-20/N-1265 hit the deceased, killing him at the spot.
The petitioners being the dependants have approached the Tribunal seeking compensation.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal after taking the evidence, by impugned judgment, awarded a sum of Rs.7,65,200/- with interest of 8% p.a.
Aggrieved by the same, the Insurance Company has filed this appeal on various grounds.

2 4.

Heard the arguments of Sri. Lakshmi Narasappa, learned counsel on behalf of Sri. A.M.
Venkatesh, learned counsel for the NC: 2023:KHC:37628 Insurance Company and Sri. Govindaraju.
K, learned counsel for petitioners No.1 and 2.
5.

It is the contention of learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the deceased was aged 65 years, he was getting only a pension of Rs.3,139/-, the accident was of the year 2016, the Tribunal has committed error in assessing the income at Rs.9,000/-, additional of future prospects of 30% is contrary to the law laid down, rate of interest at 8% is on the higher side and sought for interference.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for petitioners No.1 and 2 has contended that the deceased was working as a Daivada Paathri in the temple and earning Rs.30,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has not considered the same, the rate of interest awarded is on the lower side, it has to be enhanced to 12%, the income has to be taken at higher side and compensation has to be re-determined and sought for enhancement.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, death of the deceased on account of the accident.
The material on record did point out that the deceased was aged 65 years, he was getting a pension of Rs.3,139/-.
The Tribunal has considered that the deceased was working as a Daivada Paathri in a temple also and he was earning not less than Rs.9,000/- per month, but there is no proof before the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has considered the future prospects at 30%.

As the age of the deceased is not disputed, for a person who is aged above 60 years, there is no question of adding future prospects, therefore the finding recorded by the Tribunal to that extent needs modification.

As contended by learned counsel for the Insurance Company, the income of the deceased ought to have NC: 2023:KHC:37628 taken at Rs.3,139/- cannot be supported with, as the evidence on record did point out that the deceased was working as a Daivada Paathri in the temple and earning additional income apart from his pension.
The accident is of the year 2016.
Even if the deceased is treated as a person with no proof of income, he will earn not less than Rs.9,500/- and accordingly his notional income has to be assessed.
9. Except the wife of the deceased, the other petitioners are major sons, they cannot be treated as dependants.
Hence, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal expenses and accordingly the compensation has to be calculated.

In a case of this nature, principles of assessment of compensation is settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1 and Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2023:KHC:37628 Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2.

sentences.text: By applying these principles, compensation has to be assessed.

The income of the deceased is taken at Rs.9,500/- and for the age of 65, multiplier of '7'
has to be considered and there is no scope for considering the future prospects.

If all these factors are reconsidered, the assessment of loss of dependency will be Rs.9,500/- - Rs.3,166/- (1/3 rd) =
Rs.6,334/- x 12 x '7' multiplier = Rs.5,32,056/-.

3 consortium to wife, loss of love and affection to children, a sum of Rs.40,000/- each is assessed.
Towards funeral expenses and loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- each is assessed.
If all these are summed up, it comes to Rs.7,62,056/- as against Rs.7,65,200/- assessed by the Tribunal.

10. As regarding rate of interest is concerned, the law has been settled by the judgment of this (2009) 6 SCC 121 NC: 2023:KHC:37628 Court in the Division Bench of this court in Ms.Joyeeta Bose and Ors. -vs- Venkateshan.V. and Ors. in M.F.A.No.5896/2018 c/w M.F.A.Nos.4444/2018 and 4659/2018 (MV) DD 24.08.2020 with reference to Section 149(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Rule 253 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and Section 34 of Civil Procedure Code, at Para 52 has laid down principles regarding award of interest

, it reads thus:
"52.

Thus, under Section 34 of CPC being squarely applicable to the interest awarded by the tribunal and Section 34 empowering the tribunal to award pendente lite interest and discretion being vested with the Court/tribunal to award interest from the date of suit or petition is to the maximum extent of 6% p.a. or in other words, not exceeding 6% p.a., the contention raised by the learned Advocates appearing for the Insurance Company deserves to be accepted and accordingly, it is accepted. . . . . . . . .
. ."
10.1.

In view of the settled principles, a case of this nature shall neither be a bonanza for the petitioners nor disproportionate to the circumstances of the case and hence, the rate of interest has to be NC: 2023:KHC:37628 considered at 6% p.a. only.
Since, the difference of assessment of compensation by this Court and the Tribunal is just 0.4%, there is no reason to interfere with the order of the Tribunal.
The compensation assessed by the Tribunal is maintained as it is, but the interest shall be reduced to 6% instead of 8%.
Accordingly, the appeal merits consideration.

In the result, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.

ii) Award of Rs.7,65,200/- passed by the Tribunal is confirmed, the petitioners are entitled to the said compensation with 6% p.a. instead of 8% awarded by the Tribunal and accordingly, the order of the Tribunal is modified.
iii) Rest of the order of the Tribunal is kept intact.
iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation within eight - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:37628 weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the judgment.
v) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records forthwith.
